title: Reboarding and Role Reactivation Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview
--------
This playbook describes Redwood’s standardized process for reboarding returning employees, contractors, and role-reactivation cases (e.g., long-term leaves, role pauses, rehired alumni). It covers the people-ops tasks, security/access steps, engineering toolchain re-provisioning, expected timelines, and escalation points. The goal is a predictable, secure, and humane reboarding experience that minimizes operational friction and time-to-productivity.

Audience
--------
- People Ops / Talent Operations
- IT/Security / Access Management
- Engineering and Product Managers
- IT Help Desk and internal tools owners

Scope
-----
Applies to: full-time employees, part-time employees, contractors returning after >30 days away, and rehired alumni.
Not covered: short-term internal transfers (<30 days away) and temporary cross-functional assignments (see internal transfers doc).

Principles
----------
1. Least privilege: only grant the set of permissions required for the role at reboarding time.
2. Fast, predictable timelines: typical reboard complete within 3 business days for standard roles, 7 business days for privileged access.
3. Human-first experience: coordinate manager check-ins and a tailored reboarding checklist.
4. Auditability: every re-provisioning action must be recorded and linked to the reboarding ticket.

Quick summary (TL;DR)
---------------------
- Initiate reboard: Manager or returning employee opens a Reboarding Request in Workday (or the rehire form).
- People Ops validates: role, compensation, legal requirements, and expected start date.
- Security/IT receives auto-ticket: run automated identity checks and schedule MFA reset if required.
- Access provisioning: apply role-template in AccessEngine (see Access Templates table).
- Manager-facing tasks: confirm project assignments, invite to team Slack channel, schedule first-week 1:1s.

Reboarding SLA targets
----------------------
- Identity verification and core account reactivation: 8 business hours
- Standard tool access (Slack, email, GitHub read): 24–48 business hours
- Privileged systems (prod deploy, admin consoles): 3–7 business days and manager-approved attestations

Step-by-step reboarding workflow (detailed)
-----------------------------------------
1) Request initiation (Manager or employee)
   - Owner: Manager / People Ops
   - Action: Submit Reboarding Request in Workday or the Rehire Form within the People Ops portal. Include: start date, role, manager, office/site, remote status, requested equipment.

2) People Ops validation (Day 0–1)
   - Owner: People Ops Specialist
   - Checklist:
     - Confirm legal eligibility and compensation bands
     - Confirm background check status (if applicable)
     - Confirm manager-provided role scope and required systems
     - Select Access Template (see table below)
   - Outcome: Approve request and trigger AccessEngine ticket and IT/equipment workflow.

3) Identity & Access (Day 0–2)
   - Owner: Security / IT access team
   - Automated steps:
     - Verify identity in IDP (Okta) and re-activate login source
     - Reset primary device MFA and notify employee via secure channel
   - Manual steps:
     - Apply Access Template in AccessEngine to provision Slack, Google Workspace, Jira, GitHub (read), and internal dashboards
     - For privileged roles, create a temporary approval request to the least-privilege owner, recorded in the ticket.

4) Device and tools provisioning (Day 1–3)
   - Owner: IT Fulfillment
   - Actions:
     - Ship hardware (if requested) and open device enrollment ticket with Device Fleet Service
     - Pre-stage developer VM image if developer role (image id: dev-image-2026-v2)
     - Enroll device into MDM and verify compliance policies: disk encryption, disk passcode, EDR installed.

5) Manager reactivation checklist (Day 0–3)
   - Owner: Hiring Manager
   - Required actions:
     - Confirm first-week goals and onboarding buddy
     - Add to team calendar (standups, core syncs)
     - Create project-specific access requests (datastores, S3 buckets, API keys) via the Project Access Form

6) Final verification & kickoff (Day 1–5)
   - Owner: People Ops / Manager
   - Actions:
     - Run reboarding verification script to confirm sign-in, Slack, email, GitHub access
     - Manager schedules reboarding kickoff meeting (60 minutes) and 30/60/90 day check-ins

Automated checks and scripts
----------------------------
- reboard-verify.sh (example):
  #!/bin/bash
  set -e
  USER_EMAIL="$1"
  okta-check --user "$USER_EMAIL" || exit 2
  slack-check --user "$USER_EMAIL" || exit 3
  gcloud iam policies list --filter="email:$USER_EMAIL" || exit 4
  echo "REBOARD OK"

- The script lives in internal-tools/reboarding and is invoked by the AccessEngine workflow post-activation. Results are attached to the Workday ticket.

Access Templates (common)
-------------------------
| Template name | Default systems provisioned | Typical SLA | Notes |
|---------------|----------------------------:|------------:|-------|
| engineer-standard | Slack, Google Workspace, Jira, GitHub (read), CI read | 24–48h | Use project-level requests for repo write access |
| infra-privileged | All engineer-standard + Prod Deploy Role, SRE dashboards | 3–7d | Requires two manager approvals and security attestation |
| pm-standard | Slack, Google Workspace, Jira, Product Analytics (read) | 24–48h | Request analytics write separately |
| contractor-basic | Slack, Google Workspace (limited), Jira (limited) | 24–48h | Contractors require sponsor and signed contractor agreement |

Manager templates for project-specific access
--------------------------------------------
Managers should use the Project Access Form for additional permissions. Required information:
- Project name and purpose
- List of resources (repo URLs, bucket names, dataset ids)
- Justification and expected duration
- Reviewer/approver (owner of the resource)

Security controls and attestations
--------------------------------
- All reboards that request privileged access must include:
  1) Manager attestation of business need
  2) Security reviewer approval (via AccessEngine)
  3) Time-bound access with automatic expiry (30/90/365 days depending on role)

Escalation and exceptions
-------------------------
- If identity verification fails: People Ops escalates to Security lead within 2 business hours.
- If device enrollment fails beyond 48 hours: IT Fulfillment escalates to IT Manager.
- Exception cases (legal holds, regulatory constraints) require manual sign-off from director-level People Ops and Security. Document exception using Exception Request Template and attach to the ticket.

Manager communication templates
-------------------------------
- Slack DM to new returner (example):
  Hi <name>! Welcome back — excited for your first day on <start date>. I've added you to #team-foo and created your first-week plan. Please check the reboarding checklist in Workday and ping me if anything is missing. — <manager name>

- Email to IT when equipment needed:
  Subject: Reboarding: <Name> — Equipment Request
  Body:
  Employee: <Name>
  Role: <Role>
  Start date: <date>
  Equipment: MacBook Pro 14 / Dock / Monitor
  Shipping address: <address>
  Manager: <name>

Audit and reporting
-------------------
- People Ops will run a monthly "Reboard Completeness" report showing: requests opened, mean time to core activation, mean time to privileged access, and top failure reasons.
- Security will run quarterly audits of reactivated privileged accounts and validate time-bound expirations.

Appendices
----------
A. Typical timings and owner matrix
- Core reactivation: Security (8h)
- Standard access: IT/AccessEngine (24–48h)
- Device shipping: IT Fulfillment (3–5 business days domestic)
- Privileged access approval: Security (3–7 business days)

B. Common troubleshooting commands
- Re-run IDP sync: okta-cli sync --user <email>
- Force Slack invite: slack-cli invite --user <email> --channel <channel>
- Check GitHub org membership: gh api /orgs/redwood/memberships/<username>
